H01.summary: Keep the familiar portrait at lower left and large combat hexes in the middle.
H01.strength: Closest to the current 3D HUD; each combat state has room.
H01.tradeoff: Health and cooldowns require wider eye movement; minimap occupies a larger corner.

H02.summary: Bring the portrait, health, ammo and action states into one centered dock.
H02.strength: Recommended HUD: fewer places to look and more open battlefield.
H02.tradeoff: Keep it shallow, scalable and outside the hero's immediate movement space.

H03.summary: Check the HUD against late-run pressure and a melee character.
H03.strength: Melee replaces ammo; Burst's HP cost is visible before use.
H03.tradeoff: Horde density and effects are an art/readability target, not a measured performance result.

M01.summary: Clear jammers, restore relays and turn captured defenses into support.
M01.strength: Recommended signature mode; makes good use of existing towers, gates and routes.
M01.tradeoff: Needs ownership/objective states and pressure pacing; avoid long stationary capture timers.

M02.summary: Escort a mobile home base through route choices and blocked streets.
M02.strength: A clear reason to move, with the operation's maintenance breaks built into the fiction.
M02.tradeoff: Needs a new carrier, route behavior, repair rules and strong protection against escort frustration.

M03.summary: Fight the horde while destroying specific boss components to remove attacks.
M03.strength: Gives manual aiming and target choice a visible consequence.
M03.tradeoff: Highest bespoke art/encounter burden; melee builds need fair access to parts.

M04.summary: Choose between a safe exit and more carried salvage as the storm approaches.
M04.strength: Adds a clear push-your-luck decision to the same survivor combat.
M04.tradeoff: Needs extraction, hazard and reward rules; only carried rewards should be at risk.

F01.summary: Optional route choice inside the existing five-stage operation.
F01.strength: Support versus supplies creates a readable decision between battles.
F01.tradeoff: Branching and persistent route rewards are new proposals, not current reference behavior.

F02.summary: Present existing NIPMH buying, reserves and weighted capacity in the new dark UI.
F02.strength: Reuses a substantial existing progression system; distinguishes price from capacity.
F02.tradeoff: Three offers are shown for layout review, not a proposed limit on the stock system.

T01.summary: Seven normal hex nodes, accurate prerequisite links and a separate automatic mastery.
T01.strength: Recommended full-tree view: strongest visual connection to the combat HUD.
T01.tradeoff: Effects require selection; names and long mastery labels must stay legible at smaller sizes.

T02.summary: The same Attack build shown as cards with short effect text.
T02.strength: More information visible without hovering; easier to learn unfamiliar builds.
T02.tradeoff: Uses more screen area; less spacious than the hex layout.

T03.summary: A paused drawer for quickly spending a point on available talents.
T03.strength: Faster familiar upgrades while the full tree remains accessible.
T03.tradeoff: Optional supplement only; do not turn it into three random offers or conceal other available nodes.

T04.summary: The hex layout applied to Snow White's authored turret Skill tree.
T04.strength: Explains lasting turrets, prerequisites and the automatic Detonation mastery.
T04.tradeoff: Preview illustrations are concept aids; functional previews would be extra implementation work.

T05.summary: Scarlet's authored Burst tree with the healing payoff and HP cost shown together.
T05.strength: Demonstrates that the UI can explain character-specific tradeoffs.
T05.tradeoff: Long names require wrapping; use explicit current/max HP wording when finalizing combat rules.

T06.summary: See all three categories' owned nodes and mastery progress in one view.
T06.strength: Useful build summary; all 21 normal nodes and three capstones remain visible.
T06.tradeoff: An overview, not a replacement for prerequisite graphs and selected-node detail.
